{{Quote|This is the Jedi Holocron&hellip;given to me many years ago by a very old Jedi&hellip;before his&hellip;untimely departure.|Palpatine to Leia Organa Solo|<ref name="DE5" />}}
The '''Tedryn Holocron''', also known as '''Vodo-Siosk Baas's holocron''', the '''Holocron of''' '''Bodo Baas''', or simply the '''Jedi Holocron''', was a [[Jedi holocron/Legends|Jedi holocron]] created over four thousand years before the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], possibly by [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Tedryn]].

==Properties==
[[File:Tedryn_holocron_activating.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Leia activated the holocron by touching the design on its side.]]
{{Quote|It knows you are a Jedi.|Palpatine to Leia Organa Solo|<ref name="DE5" />}}
The [[Tedryn]] [[Holocron/Legends|Holocron]] was a glowing cube that sat comfortably in the palm of the [[Limb/Legends|hand]].<ref name="DE5E">[[Dark Empire endnotes|''Dark Empire'' endnotes]]</ref> It was a milky [[Jade/Legends|jade]] [[Crystal/Legends|crystal]] block<ref name="Descr" /> with ancient [[Writing/Legends|writings]] on its smooth surface.<ref name="DES">''[[Dark Empire Sourcebook]]'', Page 62.</ref> The Jedi teaching device<ref name="DE5" /> was an interactive wisdom source,<ref name="DE5E" /> that combined ancient organic<ref name="DES" /> crystalline formations and hardware. Its metal parts were embossed with curious designs suggesting great antiquity.<ref name="DE5E" />

The inner crystals sensed the affiliation of the [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-user]] to the [[Light side of the Force/Legends|light side]], though any [[The Force/Legends|Force]]-talented user could<ref name="DE5E" /> activate the holocron by touching the design on its side. The holocron produced a primitive<ref name="DE5" /> green-tinted<ref name="TEGTTF" /> [[Hologram/Legends|hologram]]<ref name="DE5" /> of its primary [[Gatekeeper/Legends|gatekeeper]].<ref name="TEGTTF" />

The knowledge contained in the holocron could be accessed by anyone to a certain extent. On the most superficial level the holocron was merely a recording device, a collection of records with interactive holograms of the authors.<ref name="DE5E" /> The basic knowledge in the holocron could be accessed directly, like a computer [[encyclopedia]], or by interfacing with the current gatekeeper.<ref name="DES" />

However, the greatest portion of the wisdom could be unlocked only by a [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]]. The inner organic crystals were the key to the deeper levels of knowledge. Not even [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], who possessed the device for thirty years&mdash;had the power to reach its restricted information.<ref name="DE5E" /> Deeper teachings and accounts were relayed directly by the Masters who added them to the holocron.<ref name="DES" />

The Tedryn Holocron was tailored toward helping Jedi Masters penetrate the secrets of the Force. Even beings already [[Jedi training/Legends|trained]] in the Jedi ways benefit greatly from such a source of learning.<ref name="Echoes of the Jedi">''[[Echoes of the Jedi]]'', Page 5.</ref>

==Gatekeepers==
{{Quote|Hear the words of Bodo Baas!|Bodo Baas|<ref name="DE5" />}}
The gatekeeper was a Jedi Master's holographic simulation that worked as a search and recovery engine built in every holocron. The fact that one gatekeeper relayed certain information was not an indicator that this information had been recorded by that particular gatekeeper, as the data contained within the holocron could be accessed by all gatekeepers.<ref name="TEGTTF" />

Originally, the holocron was named after '''[[Tedryn]]''', but later often was referred to as simply the Jedi Holocron, or the [[Holocron/Legends|Holocron]] of [[Bodo Baas]]. The [[New Jedi Order]] called it the Tedryn Holocron to avoid confusion over [[Vodo-Siosk Baas]] and Bodo Baas, and also to honor their predecessor. Tedryn may have been the creator and first gatekeeper of the holocron. At some point before the [[Great Sith War/Legends|Great Sith War]], Jedi Master '''[[Odan-Urr/Legends|Odan-Urr]]''', one of the gatekeepers, added a record to the holocron about the [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|Great Hyperspace War]].<ref name="TEGTTF" />

[[File:TedrynHolocron_EGTF.jpg|thumb|right|130px|[[Bodo Baas]], one of the holocron's gatekeepers]]
The Tedryn Holocron eventually passed to '''Vodo-Siosk Baas''',<ref name="TEGTTF" /> a [[Krevaaki]] Jedi Master and [[Jedi historian]].<ref name="POTJ">''[[Power of the Jedi Sourcebook]]''</ref> In [[3997 BBY]],<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> his hologram introduced the recent history of the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]], including [[Naga Sadow/Legends|Naga Sadow]] and [[Freedon Nadd]] to [[Exar Kun/Legends|Exar Kun]].<ref name="DLOTS1" /> Vodo's hologram introduced Exar Kun, [[Ulic Qel-Droma/Legends|Ulic Qel-Droma]] and the Great Sith War to the students of [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] more than [[11 ABY/Legends|four thousand years]] after his death. Later Luke asked Baas about the fate of Exar Kun, and the gatekeeper told him that Kun slew his own master, Vodo himself, when the latter tried to bring his [[Padawan/Legends|apprentice]] back from the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]]. Vodo-Siosk Baas was the last invoked gatekeeper, because the spirit of Kun destroyed the holocron before Baas could reveal Exar's fate to Skywalker.<ref name="DA" />

An auxiliary gatekeeper told stories of intrigues in the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] to the apprentices of Skywalker<ref name="IJEDI">''[[I, Jedi]]''</ref> before another gatekeeper spoke to Luke of how the young [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]] became a Jedi.<ref name="DA" />

The last gatekeeper of the Holocron was '''Bodo Baas''', a descendant of Vodo-Siosk Baas.<ref name="TEGTTF" /> His hologram explained a partial story of Ulic-Qel Droma,<ref name="DE5E" /> a brief description of the dark side, and the prophecy written by [[Bodo Baas's Master|Baas' master]].<ref name="DE6">[[Dark Empire 6|''Dark Empire'' 6]]</ref> Later Baas suggested that ancient Jedi artifacts may be found on [[Ossus/Legends|Ossus]], an old Jedi teaching center, and that they could find survivors of the [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|Great Jedi Purge]].<ref name="DE7">[[Dark Empire II 1|''Dark Empire II'' 1]]</ref> Later, in the Jedi Praxeum, Luke asked Baas to explain the power classified as [[Mind trick/Legends|Alter Mind]] to [[Corran Horn/Legends|Corran Horn]] in the apprentice's chamber.<ref name="IJEDI" />

==Contents==
According to Obi-Wan Kenobi, the Tedryn Holocron contained thousand-year-old secrets and the some of the most secret Jedi history and teachings.<ref name="DE5E" /> It held information about the origins of the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] and the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] and their earliest conflicts.<ref name="TEGTTF" />

Vodo-Siosk Baas made a recording about the war known as the [[Hundred-Year Darkness/Legends|Hundred-Year Darkness]], in which he spoke of the [[Second Great Schism]], how the [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] used the dark side to turn animals into warriors, mounts, and [[Leviathan (creature)|Leviathans]], and the [[Battle of Corbos|final confrontation on Corbos]]. By the time of the recording, the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] had learned that the [[Exiles|exiled Dark Jedi]] had conquered the [[Sith (species)/Legends|Sith species]] on [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]] and that [[Ajunta Pall]] had formed an [[Sith Empire/Legends|Empire]].<ref name="TEGTTF" />

Sometime after 5,000 BBY, Master Odan-Urr asked [[Jori Daragon]], [[Anavus Svag]] and the [[Dark Holocron]] about the [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|Great Hyperspace War]], before making a record to preserve the full story of the war for the Jedi Order. In the record he spoke of hyperspace explorers Gav and Jori Daragon of the Koros system meeting the descendants of the Exiles, who had become [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lords]]. Odan-Urr spoke of Naga Sadow launching an assault using illusions to frighten off the Republic troops. Once the Sith were defeated, Odan-Urr recovered the Dark Holocron from a ship and learned about Sadow's escape.<ref name="TEGTTF" />

At some point before the Great Sith War, when he was around a thousand years old, Ood Bnar recorded his prophecies in the holocron.<ref name="DE9">[[Dark Empire II 3|''Dark Empire II'' 3]]</ref> The device also contained information about Ood Bnar himself, the Neti species and the Ryyk planet.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Alien Species real-world book">[[The Essential Guide to Alien Species (real-world book)|''The Essential Guide to Alien Species'']], Page 88.</ref>

Jeth noted, that Nadd gave his support to the founders of the Krath: Satal and Aleema Keto.<ref name="TEGTTF" />

==History==
===Early history===
The Holocron was created sometimes before the [[Great Sith War/Legends|Great Sith War]], possibly by Jedi Master [[Tedryn]], whom the artifact was named for. Tedryn might have been the first gatekeeper of the holocron and was followed by a long line of Jedi who contributed to the Holocron. One of the early gatekeepers was Master Odan-Urr, who added a record to the holocron about the Great Hyperspace War.<ref name="TEGTTF" /> One other gatekeeper was the then thousand years old Ood Bnar, who recorded his prophecies in the Holocron.<ref name="DE9" />

By [[3997 BBY]],<ref name="NEC" /> [[Vodo-Siosk Baas]] was in possession of the Holocron and became a gatekeeper by imparting it with his knowledge and memory. One day, he found his Apprentice, Exar Kun questioning the holocron about the Dark Jedi Freedon Nadd and the Sith. Baas turned off the device, feeling that such knowledge was meant only for Jedi Masters.<ref name="DLOTS1" />

Around [[600 BBY/Legends|600 BBY]], Bodo Baas inherited the Holocron<ref name="TEGTTF" /> and reorganized every single recording.<ref name="FF">{{FactFile|74|BAA 1-2|Bodo Baas}} {{C|German version}}</ref> By [[590 BBY]],  he was part of a group of Jedi who lived in the Adega system and recorded the teachings and history of the Jedi.<ref name="DE5" />

The Holocron was believed to have gone missing hundreds of years before the [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|Great Jedi Purge]], but it was in the possession
of Ashka Boda.<ref name="DES" />

===Imperial Period===
In 19 BBY, at the beginning of the Great Jedi Purge,<ref name="TEGTTF" /> [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine's]] agents brought Jedi Masters before him to be questioned and tortured for forgotten secrets and cures, that could help him in his quest for immortality.<ref name="DE2E" /> The Tedryn Holocron was among the belongings of Bodo Baas, who was executed by the Emperor.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Characters">''[[The Essential Guide to Characters]]'', Page 9.</ref> Shortly thereafter the device came in the possession of Master Ashka Boda. The Emperor executed Boda as well, and took possession of the Tedryn Holocron. Palpatine used the secrets in the holocron to cheat death with the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] and [[Cloning/Legends|cloning]] technology,<ref name="DE2E" /> and he recorded some of the holocron's secrets in his [[The Book of Anger|''Book of Anger'']].<ref name="Dark Empire endnotes">[[Dark Empire endnotes|''Dark Empire'' endnotes]], The Book of Anger</ref> However, the greatest portion of the ancient knowledge remained hidden from the Emperor, because it was accessible only by Jedi Knights. He considered the Holocron to be only a collection of ancient records.<ref name="DE5E" /> The reborn Emperor held the artifact in his study in the [[Emperor's Citadel|Imperial Citadel]] on Byss.<ref name="DE Sourcebook">''[[Dark Empire Sourcebook]]'', Page 36.</ref>

At some later time, Obi-Wan Kenobi described the Holocron to his apprentice, Luke Skywalker. Kenobi thought the holocron could help reestablish the Jedi Order.<ref name="DE5E" />

===Rediscovery for the New Jedi Order===
[[File:Leia_Bodo.jpg|thumb|left|200px|[[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia]] listens to the teachings of the [[Holocron/Legends|holocron]].]]
In [[10 ABY/Legends|10 ABY]], [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa Solo]] was captured by the reborn Emperor on his throneworld, Byss.<ref name="DE4">[[Dark Empire 4|''Dark Empire'' 4]]</ref> The Emperor showed the Tedryn Holocron to the Jedi, trying unsuccessfully to turn her to the dark side. Leia managed to flee with the holocron.<ref name="DE5" /> Onboard the [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']] she listened to Bodo Baas's version of the downfall of Ulic Qel-Droma, and wondered whether there was hope for Luke, or if he had fallen too far to the dark side in his effort to conquer it from within.<ref name="DE5E" />

After the [[Battle of Calamari|battle of Mon Calamari]], Leia returned to [[Pinnacle Base]], where she again accessed the holocron. She asked Master Baas about her brother's future, but the gatekeeper answered that he could not tell because Skywalker's future was obscured. He then recounted a prophecy written by his own Master. Moments later, a fleet of Star Destroyers led by the ''Eclipse'' dropped out of hyperspace above the Pinnacle Moon. The Emperor demanded that Leia and the Tedryn Holocron be delivered to him; he would discuss a truce if the Rebels complied. Leia accepted his terms, but left the holocron in her chambers. Aboard the ''Eclipse'', she realized that Palpatine's hold over Luke had become too strong, and that the dark side was consuming him. The siblings dueled until Leia managed to break Palpatine's spell over Luke, and they confronted the Emperor together, fulfilling Bodo Baas's ancient prophecy.<ref name="DE6" />

Later, Luke found clues in the Tedryn Holocron indicating possible survivors of the Jedi Purge. He spent many standard weeks searching for Jedi, until eventually, he found [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] [[Kam Solusar]] on the [[Nespis VIII|Space City]] of [[Nespis VIII]]. Meanwhile, Leia spent long hours with the Tedryn Holocron while Luke was away. During one such session, Baas told her that [[Vima-Da-Boda]] could help them.<ref name="DE7" />

Luke learned from the Holocron that ancient Jedi artifacts were possibly located on [[Ossus/Legends|Ossus]]. His new ally Kam Solusar was rather unimpressed with the small cube, but he was taken aback when it sensed him and activated. The image of Baas gave some cryptic wisdom, and instructed Kam and his fellow Jedi to have patience.<ref name="DE7" /> Skywalker and Solusar traveled to Ossus, where they met Ood Bnar, a hibernating Jedi Master from Exar Kun's time, whose prophecies were stored in the Holocron.<ref name="DE9" /> With the help of the native [[Ysanna/Legends|Ysanna]], the Jedi found a Jedi library that had remained undisturbed for four thousand years.<ref name="DE10">[[Dark Empire II 4|''Dark Empire II'' 4]]</ref>

By 11 ABY, the Tedryn Holocron was kept in a small library, where Luke Skywalker's apprentices could study it.<ref name="IJEDI" /> Skywalker gathered his twelve students in the grand audience chamber of the Massassi temple on Yavin 4 for a formal opening of the Jedi Praxeum. He invoked gatekeeper Vodo-Siosk Baas to impart a teaching to his apprentices. The ancient Krevaaki Jedi Master spoke of the Great Sith War, and of Exar Kun and Ulic-Qel Droma, and he warned the students to beware of the temptations of conquest.<ref name="DA" />

Tionne Solusar studied Jedi history from the holocron in the month after arriving to the Praxeum, transcribing its data to tapes and holograms, with a sense of urgency.<ref name="TEGTTF" /> Her studies allowed her to help the other students with historical examples when the instructions of Master Skywalker were not clear enough. After Gantoris constructed a lightsaber, Corran Horn suspected that he had learned how from the Tedryn Holocron, but Luke explained to him that an inbuilt restriction mechanism prevented the user from accessing knowledge for which he or she is not ready.<ref name="IJEDI" />

After the death of Gantoris, Horn advised Master Skywalker on repeating the historical lessons of the Holocron to the students so as to instill a sense of history and purpose to the students, and make them less vulnerable for the corruption of the dark side.<ref name="IJEDI" /> Bodo Baas spoke to the Jedi hopefuls about the heroic adventures of ancient Jedi Knights and about their battles against the dark side.<ref name="DA" />

Corran Horn tried to get some information about the murder of Gantoris, and Baas explained to him that, during the Great Sith War, Yavin 4 had been the seat of power for the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] Exar Kun. Kun enslaved the Massassi and forced them to build temples in the jungle, as Naga Sadow had done before. Eventually, the Dark Lord was killed in a Jedi attack. An auxiliary gatekeeper told the students stories of court intrigue in the Old Republic without specifying the subjects of his tales.<ref name="IJEDI" />

After Corran Horn and Tionne had accessed all the information concerning Exar Kun, Luke tried to access the deeper levels of the device,<ref name="IJEDI" /> but when he asked the Vodo-Siosk Baas gatekeeper about Exar Kun's fate, the spirit of the Dark Lord, who had been imprisoned on Yavin 4 since his death four millennia earlier, interrupted Vodo-Siosk Baas by destroying the Holocron.<ref name="DA" />

Transcripts and copied data collected by Tionne Solusar and stored in the [[Jedi Archives (Ossus)|new Jedi library]] on [[Ossus/Legends|Ossus]], kept the teachings of the Tedryn Holocron alive after its destruction.<ref name="TEGTTF" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|The Tedryn Holocron is the one that Vodo is in possession of in ''Tales of the Jedi'', and he's ''one'' of the gatekeepers of it. ''One'' of the gatekeepers of the Jedi Holocron is Bodo Baas. Ood Bnar is ''another'' gatekeeper of that same Jedi Holocron.|[[Bob Cooper]] paraphrasing [[Kevin J. Anderson]]|<ref name="EE1RWlc">[[Empire's End 1|''Empire's End'' 1]] {{C|"Rebel Writers" letters column}}</ref>}}

[[February 18]], [[1992]].<ref name="DE2 Marvel">{{Marvel|url=comics/issue/54058/star_wars_dark_empire_1991_2|text=Star Wars: Dark Empire (1991) #2}}</ref> There it's referred to as an "ancient object" that Palpatine learned essence transfer from and no further information is given about what it is.<ref name="DE2E" /> It went on to be mentioned again in the endnotes for [[Dark Empire 4|''Dark Empire'' 4]],<ref name="DE5E" /> which was published on [[June 23]],[[1992]]<ref name="DE4 Marvel">{{Marvel|url=comics/issue/54060/star_wars_dark_empire_1991_4|text=Star Wars: Dark Empire (1991) #4}}</ref> and to appear in [[Dark Empire 5|''Dark Empire'' 5]],<ref name="DE5" /> which was published on [[August 18]], [[1992]]<ref name="DE5 Marvel">{{Marvel|url=comics/issue/54061/star_wars_dark_empire_1991_5|text=Star Wars: Dark Empire (1991) #5}}</ref> and in [[Dark Empire 6|''Dark Empire'' 6]],<ref name="DE6" /> which was published on [[October 20]], [[1992]].<ref name="DE6 Marvel">{{Marvel|url=comics/issue/54062/star_wars_dark_empire_1991_6|text=Star Wars: Dark Empire (1991) #6}}</ref> Throughout ''[[Star Wars: Dark Empire]]'' and the [[Dark Empire endnotes|''Dark Empire'' endnotes]], the Tedryn Holocron is referred to as "the Jedi Holocron".<ref name="DE">''[[Star Wars: Dark Empire]]''</ref><ref name="DE5E" /> It's also crawls for [[Tales of the Jedi 1|''Tales of the Jedi'' 1]], [[Tales of the Jedi 3|''Tales of the Jedi'' 3]], and [[Tales of the Jedi – The Freedon Nadd Uprising 1|''Tales of the Jedi: The Freedon Nadd Uprising'' 1]] refer to "the Jedi Holocron", which was implied to be the Tedryn Holocron by no other holocrons being known of at the time of their publication.<ref name="TOTJ1">[[Tales of the Jedi 1|''Tales of the Jedi'' 1]]</ref><ref name="TOTJ3">[[Tales of the Jedi 3|''Tales of the Jedi'' 3]]</ref><ref name="FNU1">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Freedon Nadd Uprising 1|''Tales of the Jedi: The Freedon Nadd Uprising'' 1]]</ref> However, the opening crawl for [[Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith 1|''Tales of the Jedi: Dark Lords of the Sith'' 1]] refers to the Tedryn Holocron as "his (Exar Kun's) Master's holocron" and the comic refers to a [[Dark Holocron|Sith holocron]],<ref name="DLOTS1" /> which went on to appear in [[Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith 4|''Tales of the Jedi: Dark Lords of the Sith'' 4]].<ref name="DLOTS4">[[Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith 4|''Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith'' 4]]</ref> The name "Tedryn Holocron" is used for the first time in [[Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War 1|''Tales of the Jedi: The Sith War'' 1]]<ref name="TSW1">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War 1|''Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War'' 1]]</ref> and went on to be used in ''[[The New Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology]]''<ref name="WP">''[[The New Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology]]''</ref> and [[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']].<ref name="TEGTTF" />

In ''[[The Essential Guide to Characters]]'', the holocron that appears in ''Star Wars: Dark Empire'' is said to be a different holocron than the one that appears in [[Dark Apprentice (novel)|''Dark Apprentice'']],<ref name="The Essential Guide to Characters" /> but this contradicts the text of ''Dark Apprentice''<ref name="DA" /> and therefore is assumed to be an error.
